title: $T_{E,F}$ preserves bounded constructible complexes
statement:
For a prime $\ell$, a scheme $X$, finite extensions $E\le F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb$ and
a bounded constructible complex $K$ of $E_X$-modules ([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), the
complex $T_{E,F}K$ ([def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield]) is a bounded constructible complex of
$F_X$-modules.

proof.text:
Write $G_Z=F_Z\otimes_{E_Z}-$ for the coefficient inclusion [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map]. It preserves finite limits by [lem-sfb-subfield-flat] and finite colimits by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], hence is exact. By [def-sfb-left-derived-exact], [def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield] and [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-preserves-homology],
$$H^q(T_{E,F}K)\cong G_X(H^qK).$$
The homology lemma's hypothesis holds on every scheme by the same flatness node; this does not require a bounded representative.

source.place: first sentence: exactness and the cohomology formula

proof.text: In applying finite presentations, coefficient pullback can be identified with raw module pullback: [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] gives the ring isomorphism $f^{-1}E_Z\cong E_W$ for every $f:W\to Z$, and likewise for $F$. Part (5) of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] expresses this identification as scalar extension along that isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-scalar-extension-finite-presentation] to the isomorphism and its inverse: a finite presentation on either side gives one on the other. Thus the local-presentation predicates may be checked using the coefficient pullbacks of [def-sfb-pull-iso].

source.place: local presentations: canonical identification of pulled-back coefficient rings

proof.text: Let $M$ be constructible. Choose its finite stratification and presentation covers on each stratum from [def-sfb-constructible-module] and [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. On a stratum $S$, [def-sfb-pull-iso] identifies $(G_XM)|_S$ with $G_S(M|_S)$. On every member $U\to S$ of its presentation cover, the same comparison identifies the latter restriction with $G_U(M|_U)$. By step 2 the input is finitely presented over $E_U$; [lem-sfb-internal-scalar-extension-finite-presentation] makes its extension finitely presented over $F_U$. Step 2 identifies this with the raw pulled-back-ring presentation required by the definition. Hence the same covers on the same finite stratification witness constructibility of $G_XM$.

source.place: tensoring local presentations on the same strata

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], $H^qK$ is constructible for each $q$ and zero outside one finite interval. Step 3 and the isomorphism of step 1 give constructibility of $H^q(T_{E,F}K)$: compose its local-presentation isomorphisms with that isomorphism. Since $G_X$ preserves the initial object by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], it sends zero to zero, so step 1 retains the same interval. These are exactly the two conditions in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible].

proof_origin.place: proof reassembled from the extracted finite-presentation lemma and existing comparison nodes; current general ring-object constructibility definition

This delivery does it: the item statement is verbatim the main-20261015 blueprint statement, and its stmt_deps are unchanged. The proof is now 2307 characters in 4 steps, and the new node's proof in words in the report is 1185 characters. Step 1: lem-sfb-subfield-flat gives finite limits on every scheme and change-of-scalars (2) gives finite colimits, so the extension is exact. def-sfb-left-derived-exact then gives L(Ext) ≅ D(Ext), and the homology lemma gives H^q(TK) ≅ G_X(H^qK); its every-scheme hypothesis is met. Step 2: module pullback is Ext_{α_f}∘mapMod(f^*), which is compared with the raw mapMod(g^*) used in def-sfb-constructible-module and def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented. sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients (1) says α_f is invertible for E and F with no condition on ell, change-of-scalars (5) gives Ext_α ≅ Res_{α^{-1}}, and the new lemma applied in both directions transfers finite presentation. This is a correct elementary application of cited statements. Step 3: def-sfb-pull-iso is applied along the stratum immersion and then along the cover member, keeping the same finite stratification and the same covers; no qcqs or Noetherian hypothesis is added. Step 4: Ext(0)=0 keeps the cohomological interval, and constructibility is iso-invariant. The coefficient map is p_X^* of the condensed inclusion E→F (def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map), the same a_X as in the pull-iso and homology nodes. The new node lem-sfb-internal-scalar-extension-finite-presentation is true: Ext preserves finite colimits, and lem-weil-pbc-regular-extension-comparison gives Ext(R) ≅ S. I tested it on Z→Z/2 with M=Z/2, on M=0, m=0 and φ=id. Its hypotheses match def-sfb-finitely-presented-module and change-of-scalars (2), with sheaf-tensor (2) giving right exactness. It is self-contained, strictly smaller than the item (no D1 problem), and statement-only as B1 requires. Its searches cover the three kinds, and SheafOfModules.Presentation.map is correctly rejected as a different encoding. I searched the whole snapshot DAG and no node states it. I accept the declared tool uses: subfield-flat, the homology lemma and cartesian-coefficients. The item is not on the route-pivot drop list and nothing cites SGA.
